note: How the red and green lines' stations are laid out, for tools/build-stations.ts (see there for the format). Each is read from Albert Guillaumes' drawing of the station (estacions.albertguillaumes.cat, used as a reference only), with its exits at OpenStreetMap's subway entrances. T-Centralen, Odenplan and Fridhemsplan aren't here: they are his 3D models (public/data/stations.json).

Östermalmstorg.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the south-west end, escalators climb in two flights to a long ticket hall under Stureplan with four exits; from the north-east end, two flights to the hall at Sibyllegatan and Nybrogatan.

Gamla stan.note: Two island platforms at ground level, a metre or two above the streets beside them, red on the inner side of each and green on the outer. Stairs go down through each platform to the ticket hall under the tracks, and up from it to the streets.

Slussen.note: Two island platforms, red on the inner side of each and green on the outer. Stairs up from each platform to the hall over the tracks, at street level by Ryssgården.

Mariatorget.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. Escalators climb from each end to a ticket hall, and stairs to the street.

Zinkensdamm.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, joined in the middle. From there stairs and an escalator climb over the southern hall to the ticket hall.

Hornstull.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the west end, escalators and stairs climb to a ticket hall with exits round Hornstull; from the east end, a long flight to Långholmsgatan.

Liljeholmen.note: Three tracks in a concrete box under the bus terminal. Stairs climb from both platforms to a hall across the tracks at the north-east end, by the shopping centre.

Karlaplan.note: An island platform deep in the rock. Escalators climb from each end of it to a ticket hall: Valhallavägen to the north-east, Karlaplan to the south-west.

Gärdet.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. Escalators climb from the south-west end to Brantingsgatan; from the north-east end, escalators and stairs climb over the eastern hall to a ticket hall, with lifts up to the hill above and a long passage out to Tegeluddsvägen.

Ropsten.note: The line's northern end, high over Ropsten's bus square: two viaducts, each with one track and a platform on the side towards the other, an open gap between them. At the south-west end the two platforms are joined in a covered concourse. From its end escalators and stairs go down in the gap to the ticket hall on the ground beneath, a crossbridge with a lift crosses the gap halfway along, and another at the north-east end leads to the glazed hall over Lidingöbanan's stop, where escalators and stairs go down to the trams. The platforms' railings and roofs are drawn by src/detail/ropsten-station.ts. Positions from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and Lantmäteriet's laser scan (2021).

Stadion.note: An island platform, its rock left standing in two long pillars down the middle. From the north end a long flight climbs to a ticket hall under Valhallavägen with exits to both sides of it and to the Stadion; from the south end, escalators climb to Karlavägen.

Tekniska högskolan.note: A long island platform. Escalators climb from each end of it: to the south-east, a ticket hall under Valhallavägen with exits to the bus terminal and Roslagsbanan; to the north-west, one under Odengatan.

Universitetet.note: An island platform under the university's campus. Escalators climb from its south end to the ticket hall and the exit by Frescati.

Bergshamra.note: Two platform halls far apart, one for each track, joined by passages. From the northern one, escalators climb over the western hall to the ticket hall at Bergshamra torg.

Danderyds sjukhus.note: An island platform in a concrete box just under the ground. Escalators climb from each end to a ticket hall: by the hospital to the south, and to the bus terminal to the north.

Mörby centrum.note: The line's northern end: a wide island platform deep in the rock. Long escalators climb from it to the ticket hall under the shopping centre.

Midsommarkransen.note: Two platform halls far apart, one for each track, joined at the north-east end. From there escalators climb over each hall to an exit on either side of Svandammsvägen.

Telefonplan.note: An island platform in the open, narrowing to the east. At its west end stairs climb along it and over the northern track to the ticket hall.

Hägerstensåsen.note: An island platform in the open, its south-west end on a bridge. Stairs go down from that end to a ticket hall under the bridge, and up from the other end to one over the tracks.

Västertorp.note: A wide island platform in the open. Stairs go down from each end to a ticket hall under the tracks.

Fruängen.note: The end of T14: an island platform in the open. At its south end the ticket hall opens onto Fruängstorget, with stairs down to Fruängsplan.

Aspudden.note: An island platform in the rock. Escalators climb from its west end to the ticket hall at Hägerstensvägen.

Örnsberg.note: An island platform in the open. At its east end stairs climb to a ticket hall over the tracks, level with the street up the slope.

Axelsberg.note: An island platform in the open. At its east end stairs climb to a ticket hall over the tracks, level with Hägerstensvägen.

Mälarhöjden.note: An island platform deep in the hill. Escalators climb from its north-east end, and a long passage runs out through the hillside to the exit at its foot.

Bredäng.note: A long island platform, its east end on a bridge over the road. Stairs go down from there to the ticket hall under the bridge.

Sätra.note: Two platforms in a cutting, facing each other across a wide paved space. At the south end the ticket hall opens onto Sätra torg.

Skärholmen.note: An island platform in a concrete box under the centre. Escalators climb from it to two ticket halls: to Skärholmen centrum in the middle, and to the bus terminal at the east end.

Vårberg.note: An island platform in the open. At its west end stairs climb to a ticket hall over the tracks, level with the street. OpenStreetMap has no entrance mapped here.

Vårby gård.note: A wide island platform on a bank, its north end on a bridge. At its south end the ticket hall opens onto the street.

Masmo.note: A short island platform deep under the hill, at the foot of its slope. Escalators climb from it straight to the ticket hall.

Fittja.note: A wide island platform on a bank. At its north-east end the ticket hall opens onto Fittja centrum.

Alby.note: Two platform halls in the rock, one for each track, joined at the east end. From there escalators climb over the southern hall to the ticket hall by the bus terminal.

Hallunda.note: A wide island platform in the open. At its east end stairs climb to a ticket hall over the tracks, and stairs on up the hill to Hallunda centrum.

Norsborg.note: The end of T13: an island platform in the open. At its east end the ticket hall opens onto the street.

Hötorget.note: An island platform deep under Sveavägen, with three ticket halls: one over the middle of the platform, under the street at Hötorget, and one at each end.

Rådmansgatan.note: An island platform 150 m long under Sveavägen (1952), one row of yellow-tiled columns down its middle. From its south end escalators climb 4.3 m to the southern ticket hall under the street, a lift beside them; through the gates passages lead west under the crossing with Rådmansgatan, past Sture V Nilsson's Strindberg wall (1983), to stairs up into the ground floor of the corner building, and east to stairs up into the glass pavilion on the eastern pavement, and a lift climbs to its tower on the western pavement. From its north end escalators climb 5.6 m to the northern ticket hall, an inclined lift beside them (the lift itself isn't walked); through the gates passages lead north-west to stairs up into the small glazed house at the park's corner, a lift beside them climbing to its tower, and north-east under the crossing with Rehnsgatan to stairs up into the ground floor of the corner building, Sveavägen 98. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights, lifts, halls and passages), the elevation model (the street 7.2 to 7.4 m above the platform at the south end, 8.5 to 9.1 m at the north end), Google's 3D mesh (the pavilion, the house's shape and the lift towers, the southern one 3.6 m south of OpenStreetMap's lift) and photographs (1955, 2005–2023); the halls' columns and booth are placed from photographs, and the pavilion's doors are inferred.

Sankt Eriksplan.note: An island platform in a concrete box under Sankt Eriksgatan. Escalators climb from each end to a ticket hall: three exits round Sankt Eriksplan to the south, one to the north.

Thorildsplan.note: An island platform in the open. At its east end stairs go down to a ticket hall under the tracks, with passages out to either side of the line.

Kristineberg.note: An island platform on a bank. At its west end stairs go down to the ticket hall at the street.

Alvik.note: Two side platforms, with the Nockebybanan's tracks between them. At their west end stairs go down from each to the ticket hall at Alviks torg; at the east end stairs climb from the northern one to Tranebergsvägen up the hill.

Stora mossen.note: An island platform in the open. At its east end stairs go down to the ticket hall under the tracks, with exits to either side.

Abrahamsberg.note: An island platform in the open. At its west end stairs go down to the ticket hall under the tracks.

Brommaplan.note: An island platform in the open. At its west end stairs go down to the ticket hall at Brommaplan.

Åkeshov.note: Two island platforms, with the track between them where the T17 turns. At their east end stairs go down from each to a passage under the tracks, with an exit on each side. (OpenStreetMap maps no entrance here.)

Ängbyplan.note: An island platform on a curve in the open. At its west end stairs go down to the ticket hall at the street. (OpenStreetMap maps no entrance here.)

Islandstorget.note: An island platform in a cutting. At its west end stairs climb to the ticket hall over the tracks, which opens onto the street up the slope by Islandstorget.

Blackeberg.note: An island platform in a cutting. At its north-west end stairs climb to a ticket hall over the tracks, with exits to Blackebergs torg and both sides of Vinjegatan.

Råcksta.note: An island platform in the open. At its north end stairs go down to the ticket hall under the tracks.

Vällingby.note: A wide island platform, its west end under the deck of Vällingby centrum. Escalators climb from that end to the ticket hall in the centre, with exits onto its squares; at the east end stairs go down to the street.

Johannelund.note: Two side platforms in the open. In the middle stairs go down from each to a passage under the tracks, which leads out to the north.

Hässelby gård.note: An island platform on a viaduct. At its west end stairs go down through the platform to the ticket hall under the tracks, at the street.

Hässelby strand.note: The western end of the line: a wide island platform in the open. At its west end stairs go down to the ticket hall under it, which opens onto the street below.

Medborgarplatsen.note: An island platform 145 m long in the concrete box of the 1933 tram tunnel under Götgatan, its northern third the vaulted lengthening of 1950. From its south end an escalator and stairs side by side climb 4.1 m to the ticket hall under the crossing with Folkungagatan; through the gates passages lead east and west under the street to stairs up into the ground floors of the corner buildings, the hotel at Folkungagatan 47 and Medborgarhuset at 45, the western one curving past Mari Pårup's mosaics (1997). Near the middle of the platform an escalator climbs north and stairs climb south to a landing under the street, a lift beside them; from it an escalator and stairs, a lift beside them, climb 3.9 m into the glass pavilion in Björns trädgård (1995), its gates just inside its doors. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (2025; its platform is drawn in the wrong place, so its flights are set on the real one), the elevation model (the street 7.8 to 8.0 m above the platform at the three entrances) and photographs (2009–2025); the landing's layout is inferred.

Skanstull.note: An island platform 180 m long in the concrete box of the old tram tunnel under Götgatan (1933, lengthened for the metro in 1950). At its south end an escalator and stairs side by side, and a lift beside them, climb 3.55 m to a low ticket hall under the street, just above the trains; through the gates a lift rises to Götgatan's median, a passage leads east over the northbound track and down a few steps into a sunken court with stairs up to the pavement at each end, one of them in a glass stair house with a lift beside it, and a passage leads south-west under the building on the corner and Ringvägen to a glass stair house on Ringvägen's north side and to open stairs at its south-west corner. At the north end stairs lead down under the southbound track to a passage west, and three escalators climb 10.2 m to the hall under the end of Allhelgonagatan, whose glass front, under the street's railing, opens onto Götgatan. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights, lifts, gates, passages and entrances), the laser scan (the court's floor 2.6 m over the platform and the pavement round it at 4.6 m; Allhelgonagatan's end 3.2 m above Götgatan's pavement; the stair houses' roofs; the open stairs at Ringvägen) and photographs (2013).

Gullmarsplan.note: Two island platforms where the line divides, the southern half of each under the deck that carries Johanneshovsvägen over the tracks and its southern end under the bus terminal beyond it. From the south end of each, stairs and an escalator side by side climb into the terminal, and a lift from its very end; through the gates the way out is north through the terminal's doors onto the square on the deck. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 62 m to 73 m south of the platforms' middle, the lifts at 73 m, the gates at 76 m, the doors at 61 m), the laser scan (the deck and the square, 4.4–5.2 m over the platforms; the terminal from 61 m to 83 m south) and photographs (2008 to 2025).

Skärmarbrink.note: Two island platforms in the open where the Farsta and Skarpnäck branches part. At their south-east ends glass stair houses climb from each platform to the ticket hall on its bridge over the tracks, and a lift from each; from the gates the way out is through the hall's doors onto the footbridge in front of it, south-west to Pelargatan or north-east over Palandergatan. From the laser scan (the hall from 65 m to 74 m south-east of the platforms' middle, its floor and the footbridge's 4.7 m over the platforms, the footbridge rising to 5.05 m at its south-western end and falling to 4.36 m at its north-eastern), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 56 m to 65 m, the lifts at 68 m and 70 m, the gates at 72 m) and photographs (2008 to 2025).

Hammarbyhöjden.note: An island platform in the open (1958, rebuilt 2003), with a ticket hall at each end. At the west end, a stair house beyond the platform's end between the tracks: the stairs go down its north half, and a corridor along its south half leads to the lift, to the ticket hall under the tracks; from the gates the way out is through the hall's glass front onto the underpass, up a few steps to Finn Malmgrens plan or on to Tidaholmsplan. At the east end, a walkway between the tracks goes down to a glass house between the bridges, and the stairs and a lift in a brick tower go down to the hall at the street, its door onto Ulricehamnsvägen. From the laser scan (the west stair house's roof 3 m over the platform from 73.4 m to 89.5 m west, the walkway 2 m down at 132 m east, the street 8.5 m under the platform at the hall's door), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the gates at 98 m west, the lifts at 83 m west and 145 m east, the east flights and the door) and photographs (2009 to 2025).

Björkhagen.note: An island platform on a bank (1958), with a glass hall on the platform in its middle. From the glass hall an escalator and stairs go down a long well to the ticket hall under the platform's northern part, and a lift runs down to it from the platform beyond the glass hall; from the gates the way out is through the hall's glass front onto the underpass under the tracks, west to Falsterbovägen and east to Malmövägen. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the glass hall's doors 17 m south of the platform's middle, the escalator and stairs from 5.4 m to 22.6 m north, the lift at 28.7 m, the gates at 30.5 m, the hall's door at 38.2 m), the laser scan (the ground at the underpass 4.9 m under the platform) and photographs (2008 to 2026).

Kärrtorp.note: An island platform in the open, beside Kärrtorps centrum. At its south end a glazed stair house stands between the tracks: two escalators and stairs go down it to the ticket hall at the street, under and between the tracks' two bridges, and a corridor along its east side leads to the lift. From the gates the way out is through the hall's doors onto Kärrtorpsplan. From the laser scan (the stair house from 73 m to 90 m south of the platform's middle, the lift's tower at 94 m, the street 6.3 m under the platform) and photographs (2007 to 2021).

Bagarmossen.note: An island platform in the rock, 19 m down. From a lobby at its north end three escalators climb 32 m to the ticket hall in the pavilion on Bagarmossen's square, an inclined lift beside them (its car at the lobby; the lift itself isn't walked); from the gates the way out is through the doors at the pavilion's point. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the escalators and the lift climbing from the platform's north end, the ticket validators at the tall part's front), the laser scan (the street 18.6 m over the platform, the pavilion's axis 9° from the platform's) and photographs (2014 to 2022).

Skarpnäck.note: The end of the green line: an island platform in a cave 25 m down, the tracks running on past its south end to buffers. At its north end stairs, an escalator and a lift climb 4.4 m to a landing over the platform; from it a passage leads west into the rock to the foot of three long escalators, an inclined lift beside them, which climb 20.5 m to the ticket hall in the brick station building on Skarpnäcks allé; from the gates the way out is through its glass front under the deep canopy. From OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the short flights and the lift at the platform's north end, the passage, the long escalators and the inclined lift, the building and its door), the laser scan (the street 24.9 m over the platform, the building's two parts and its clerestory) and photographs (2008 to 2022).

Blåsut.note: An island platform on the bank, under a butterfly roof over its southern half. At its south end the platform runs into the station's hall between the tracks, over the cycle path's underpass: the ticket gates, then stairs down along its east side and a walkway along its west side to a glass lift, both to the underpass, which comes out towards Blåsutvägen to the west and Fyrvaktarkroken to the east. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Sandsborg.note: An island platform on the bank, under a flat red steel roof over its southern half. At its south end the platform runs into the station's hall between the tracks, over the underpass of Stora Gungans väg: the ticket gates, then stairs down along its west side and a walkway along its east side to a lift, both to the underpass, which comes out on Stora Gungans väg to the west and towards Dalens allé to the east. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Skogskyrkogården.note: An island platform in the open, by the cemetery, its north end on the tracks' bridges over Sockenvägen. There the platform runs on into a glass building between the bridges: a walkway at the platform's level on its west side out to a lift, and stairs down on its east side, both to the ticket hall at the street, with the gates and the door towards Sockenvägen. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Tallkrogen.note: An island platform on the bank, under a butterfly roof over its south half, which also covers a narrow hall on the platform with the ticket gates and a lift. Beyond the hall a glass stair house between the tracks, with two flights of stairs down to the door onto Victor Balcks väg under the tracks' bridges; the lift goes down to a passage under the western track out to Tallkrogsvägen. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station.

Gubbängen.note: An island platform at ground level on the hillside, under a long butterfly roof, the track on a low bank. At its south end a short hall with the ticket gates, then stairs down southwards to a passage under the tracks, with a way out on each side. At its north end a glass stair house, with an escalator and stairs up to the ticket hall on the Herrhagsvägen bridge, which opens onto the street to the east. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, Google's 3D mesh and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Hökarängen.note: An island platform out in the open on a long curve, under a butterfly roof. At its south end a glass hall with the ticket gates, then stairs down to a passage under the tracks, with a way out on each side. At its north end the platform runs on, narrowing, into a glass stair house, with an escalator and stairs down to the ticket hall under the track's bridge, which opens towards Örbyleden. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Farsta.note: An island platform on the viaduct over Munkforsplan and Kroppaplan, under a long W-shaped roof. Two glass halls on the platform each stand over an escalator and a wide stair down towards the middle, to the ticket hall under the tracks; between them a lift. The ticket gates are in the hall's west wall, and beyond them a passage runs west between shops through the building on Farsta torg, with a way out to Kroppaplan on its north side; to the east a short way out under the viaduct comes out on Larsbodavägen. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Farsta strand.note: The end of T18: an island platform in a long, low box under Centrumhuset and Stieg Trenters torg, where the line once ran in an open cutting. In the middle two flights, each stairs beside an escalator, climb towards each other to the ticket hall in the pavilion on the square, with a lift between them; the ticket gates are on the hall's east side, and the way out is on the square, by the kiosk. Laid out from OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping, Lantmäteriet's laser scan and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Globen.note: An island platform in a cutting between Palmfeltsvägen and the tram's platform, under a long butterfly roof that widens with the platform towards its east end. At the east end escalators and stairs climb in a glazed house to the ticket hall on Globenbron, its gates in the middle, and out onto the bridge; at the west end stairs climb in a glazed tube to a small hall on Slakthusbron, its gates at the top. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Enskede gård.note: An island platform on the bank, under a butterfly roof. At its north end the platform runs on into a glass stair house between the tracks: a walkway at the platform's level along its west side out to a lift, and stairs down along its east side, both to the ticket hall in the bank, with the gates, and on into the footway's underpass under the tracks, which comes out towards Odelbergsvägen to the west and Palmfeltsvägen to the east. Laid out from Lantmäteriet's laser scan, OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping and photographs of the station; Albert Guillaumes' drawing agrees.

Sockenplan.note: An island platform on the bank, curving towards its south end. At its north end it runs into a glass stair house between the tracks, where they go onto their bridges over the square: a walkway on the platform's level out to a lift on its west side, stairs down on its east, both to the ticket hall under the bridges at the street, its doors to the north. From the laser scan (the house from 73.5 m to 91 m north, the hall's roof between the bridges to 101 m, the street 5 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the stairs from 76 m to 89 m, the lift at 88 m, the gates at 93 m) and photographs (2018).

Svedmyra.note: An island platform on a bank at its south end and on a concrete viaduct from its middle north, over the square and the street. Two long flights of stairs go down from the platform, one from its south half and one from under the roof's north end, and a lift from its middle, to the ticket hall under the viaduct at the street; from its gates a passage runs east under the tracks to the low entrance building at the foot of the bank, its doors under a curved canopy onto the square. From the laser scan (the street 6.1 m under the platform, the lift's head through the roof 13 m north, the entrance building's roof), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 14 m south down to the hall and from 38 m north down to 25 m, the lift at 14 m, the gates at 7 m) and photographs (2009 to 2024).

Stureby.note: An island platform on a low bank, entered only from its west end. There a glass stair house stands on the platform: a flight down along its south side and a lift at its west end, to the ticket hall under the concrete deck that carries the tracks west of the platform, between them at the street. From the gates the way out is through the hall's west doors into the footway under the deck, out to Munksjövägen on the south and Sågverksgatan on the north. From the laser scan (the deck's edges and the streets 4.45 m under the platform, the stair house's roof and the lift's tower), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flight from 75 m to 87 m west, the lift at 86 m, the gates at 98 m, the footway at 114 m) and photographs (2008 to 2018).

Bandhagen.note: An island platform on a bank, its south end on a bridge over Trollesundsvägen, where a glazed hall stands between the tracks' decks: an escalator, and stairs beside it, go down its west side to the ticket hall under it at the street, and a walkway along its east side leads to the lift. From the gates the way out is through the doors in the hall's south front onto Bandhagsplan. From the laser scan (the platform from 76 m south of its middle to 73 m north, the glazed hall's roof from 72 m to 97 m south, the lift's tower at 104 m, the ticket hall's roof from 85 m to 114 m and the street 6.4 m under the platform), Swedish Wikipedia (the entrance from Bandhagsplan) and photographs (2009 to 2018).

Högdalen.note: Two island platforms in a shallow cutting, a middle track to the depot between them that no train stops at. At their south ends each runs into a stair house under the library's building: in the western one stairs and a lift, in the eastern one an escalator, stairs and a lift, up to the ticket hall in the building at the street. From the gates the way out is south through its doors onto Högdalsgången. From the laser scan (the platforms 145 m long, the stair houses' roofs climbing with the stairs from the platforms' roofs to the building, the building from 94 m to 112 m south of the platforms' middle, the street 5.6 m over the platforms), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights from 79 m to 92 m south, the gates at 103 m) and photographs (2008 to 2026).

Rågsved.note: An island platform on a bank, its south-western end on a bridge over the passage under the tracks. Under its W-shaped roof a glazed stair house: an escalator, and stairs beside it, go down from its north-eastern door to the ticket hall at the street under the platform, and from the gates the way out is through the doors in the hall's south-western front onto the passage. A lift in a glazed tower at the roof's south-western end goes down to the hall. From the laser scan (the platform from 58 m south-west of its middle to 90 m north-east, the roof from 19 m south-west to 49 m north-east, the passage 6.95 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap's indoor mapping (the flights, the gates at 27 m south-west, the lift at 19 m) and photographs (2008 to 2025).

Hagsätra.note: The end of T19 (1960): a wide island platform out in the open, the tracks on bridges at its south-eastern end. From the roof's south-eastern end a ramp goes down a well in the middle of the platform, and a stair hall beyond it, between two flights of stairs, to the ticket hall under the tracks, where the lift (2011, in place of a moving walkway) comes down in a glass shaft; from the gates the way out is through the hall's glass front onto the passage under the tracks, to Hagsätra torg. From the laser scan (the well from 27.5 m south-east of the platform's middle to 63.5 m, the stair hall's roof falling from 3 m over the platform to the ticket hall's, the passage 4 m under the platform), OpenStreetMap and photographs (2018).

Kungsträdgården.note: The end of the blue line, 34 m down: two platform halls in one great cavern, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the west end, escalators climb in two flights to the ticket hall under Jakobsgatan; from the east end, two flights to the hall in Kungsträdgården park.

Rådhuset.note: Two platform halls in the rock under Kungsholmen, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the west end, escalators climb in two flights to a ticket hall with exits on Hantverkargatan and Kungsholmsgatan; from the east end, two flights and a long passage to Kungsholmsgatan.

Stadshagen.note: Two platform halls, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the south-east end, escalators climb to the ticket hall at Kellgrensgatan and the sports ground; from the north-west end, to Mariedalsvägen.

Västra skogen.note: Where the line splits for Hjulsta and Akalla: three tracks in the rock, the trains into town on the two eastern ones, beside two platform halls joined at both ends and in the middle; the trains out of town on the western track, beside its own platform, reached by stairs and a footbridge over the tracks. From the south end, escalators climb 7 m, then the metro's longest, 66 m and 33 m high, to the one exit.

Huvudsta.note: An island platform in the rock, 25 m down. Escalators climb in two flights from its west end to the ticket hall at Huvudsta centrum.

Solna strand.note: An island platform in the rock, 28 m down. Escalators climb from its north end to the ticket hall at Solna strand.

Sundbybergs centrum.note: An island platform in the rock, 26 m down. From its south end escalators climb to a ticket hall with exits round Sundbyberg's centre; from the north end, to Prästgårdsgatan.

Duvbo.note: An island platform in the rock, 20–35 m down. From its south-east end escalators climb in two flights to the ticket hall at Duvbo.

Rissne.note: Two platforms in the rock, side by side between the tracks, joined along their middle. Escalators climb between them to the ticket hall at Rissne's centre.

Rinkeby.note: Two platforms in the rock, each outside its track, with the link to Rissnedepån between them (not drawn). From the south-east end of each, escalators climb over the tracks to a landing, and on to the ticket hall at Rinkebytorget.

Tensta.note: An island platform in the rock, 20–22 m down. Escalators climb from both ends: to the ticket hall at Tensta centrum in the east, and to Hjulstavägen in the west.

Hjulsta.note: The end of T10: an island platform in the rock under Hjulstaskolan, the tracks running on beyond it. From its south-east end escalators climb to a landing, and a passage leads over the tracks to the ticket hall at Hjulsta torg.

Solna centrum.note: Two platform halls in the rock under Skytteholmsparken, 27–36 m down, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the middle, escalators climb south to the ticket hall at Centralvägen and the bus terminal; from the north end, to the hall at the shopping centre.

Näckrosen.note: Two platform halls in the rock under the old film studios, 21 m down, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. Escalators climb from both ends: to Storskogstorget in Sundbyberg in the north, and to Råsundavägen in Solna in the south.

Hallonbergen.note: An island platform in the rock, 28 m down; a third track beside it, which the trains use only to and from Rissnedepån, isn't drawn. From its north-west end escalators climb to the ticket hall at Hallonbergen's centre.

Kista.note: The only station of the blue line in the open: a wide island platform on Kistaviadukten. From its north end stairs go down to the ticket hall under the viaduct, at the bus terminal.

Husby.note: An island platform in the rock under Husby centrum. Escalators climb in two flights from both ends, to the ticket halls at Trondheimsgatan in the south and Bergengatan in the north.

Akalla.note: The end of T11: two platform halls in the rock, 20 m down, one for each track, joined at both ends and in the middle. From the north-west end, escalators climb to the ticket hall at Akalla torg and its underground bus terminal; from the south-east end, to Sibeliusgången.
